memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Yet Pharaoh's heart became hard and he would not listen to them, just as the Lord had said. Then the Lord said to Moses, "Pharaoh's heart is unyielding; he refuses to let the people go."" - Exodus 7:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh has just watched a staff become a snake and swallow his magicians' snakes. He saw it with his own eyes. And his heart became hard.

This should correct a common assumption. We often think that if people just saw enough evidence, they would believe. Pharaoh had evidence. He had a miracle in his own throne room.

Jesus made this point in a parable, where Abraham says that if people will not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be convinced even if someone rises from the dead (Lk 16:31). And indeed, when Jesus did rise, many still refused.

Unbelief is not primarily an information problem. It is a heart problem. That is humbling for those of us who think we can argue someone into the kingdom, and it is freeing too — the outcome was never resting on our cleverness.

So keep speaking, keep loving, and keep praying. But pray for hearts, not just for minds.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I trying to argue someone into faith rather than praying for their heart?
2. Where have I seen God clearly and still resisted obeying Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, soften hard hearts — including my own. Help me to pray for people rather than merely debate with them. Amen.
